summary: The outcome panel is now a text area plus one tab control, OutcomeTabs. It has two tabs, Largest files and "Unreadable folders (N)"; the unreadable tab only appears when N>0 and is never selected by the window itself. The four trigger-driven Grid rows, the Expander and both lists' own MinHeights are gone, so a new section is one TabItem and adds no row and no MinHeight. The fit at 560x644 is now written into the XAML comment: text cap 76 + margin 10 + tabs minimum 154 = 240 of 250 px, leaving 10 px to spare. EnsureSelectedTabIsVisible() is one helper that names no section; it runs once per batch (scan start, each ending), and HideSection moves the selection off a tab before collapsing it. The report gains OutcomeTabs, LargestFilesTab and UnreadableTab keys and keeps UnreadableExpander as an alias. The hook's expand mode now selects the unreadable tab, and nine new window cases S-001..S-009 feed the design's cases C-002..C-011. Finding about the build-check stage: its "the WPF exe hangs in this sandbox" diagnosis was wrong. artifacts/publish held a stale 359 KB framework-dependent apphost, and this machine has no .NET 10 runtime installed, so the host waited on its missing-runtime dialog. WindowCases' Update-App never replaced it because the exe was newer than the sources. After a real publish (140 MB single-file) the app and every window case run here.

files.why: OutcomePanel is now two rows: the texts, and OutcomeTabs holding LargestFilesTab and UnreadableTab. Everything else is keyed to one condition, whether OutcomeTabs is visible: the texts are capped at 76 px while tabs show, they get a star row (and scroll) when no tab shows, and the panel stretches while tabs show. OutcomeTabs.MinHeight is 154. The layout comment is rewritten with the fit arithmetic and 10 px headroom, the rule for adding a section, the one-row strip rule, and the no-ScrollViewer-around-a-list reason with the spike numbers.

Adds EnsureSelectedTabIsVisible (generic: select the first visible tab, collapse OutcomeTabs when none is visible), HideSection (move the selection off a tab before collapsing it) and HideUnreadable. The unreadable header is set as 'Unreadable folders (N)'. The Expander handling and OnOutcomeTextsSizeChanged are deleted.

Adds schema-1 keys OutcomeTabs{visible,selected,actualHeight,stripRows}, and LargestFilesTab and UnreadableTab{visible,selected,inView,actualHeight,header}. UnreadableExpander is kept as an alias read from UnreadableTab (expanded == selected). Documents that a list in an unselected tab reads inView false and fullRows 0.

expand mode now selects UnreadableTab, logs tabsHeight, and with FSA_HOOK_BACK goes back to the first tab. New hide mode (collapses LargestFilesTab and calls the window's guard). New variables: FSA_HOOK_MAXIMIZE, and for rescan FSA_HOOK_READABLE, FSA_HOOK_BEFORE and FSA_HOOK_AFTER. The 'drives in' line now logs the laid-out window size and state.
Selects UnreadableTab where it used to open the Expander, so the unreadable list is in the visual tree before its row is looked up.

C-001 now asserts the tab state when there are no unreadable folders. CheckLargestFiles, CheckBothLists, B-003, B-007, B-008 and Invoke-StoppedEnding are repointed to tabs, and CheckTabsKeptHeight is added. New cases S-001..S-009 for SL-065, plus helpers (New-SectionsTree, CheckFit, Invoke-Sized, CheckMaximized), the new hook variables and the All roster.

Adds plant rows S09 (ListBox) and S10 (TreeView, with a blank line in between). Each plants a list on the line after a ScrollViewer, pinned to fitness offset 0, proving the (?s) rule matches across a line break.

obligations.how: WindowCases C-001 (a small tree, no unreadable folders) now asserts: OutcomeTabs visible and selected=LargestFilesTab; UnreadableTab.visible=false; the UnreadableExpander alias is still emitted with visible=false and expanded=false; UnreadableList.inView=false; stripRows=1. It passed in the full suite.

S-001: 104 files and 1 denied folder at 560x644, with 26 extra drive buttons and the reveal status line shown. Largest files is selected with ≥1 full row. UnreadableTab reads visible, header 'Unreadable folders (1)', not selected. UnreadableList.inView=false, stripRows=1, texts 76 px (the cap), tabs 164 px (154 minimum + 10 spare), and 0 px left over in the panel. Passed.

S-002, two runs at the floor. (1) Select UnreadableTab: LargestFilesList reads inView=false, fullRows=0 with its old height of 98.12 px, and OutcomeTabs stays 164 px before and after. (2) Select, lay out, go back: UnreadableList reads inView=false, fullRows=0 with its old height of 136.04 px, and OutcomeTabs is unchanged. Passed.

S-003: rescan with FSA_HOOK_BEFORE=UnreadableTab (the list was on screen, 136.88 px), and FSA_HOOK_READABLE deleting the one denied folder, so the second scan finds N=0. The second ending shows UnreadableTab hidden, the alias not shown, and OutcomeTabs.selected=LargestFilesTab. UnreadableList is off screen with 0 rows; LargestFilesList shows its new rows. Passed.

This state cannot happen in the app: LargestFilesTab is shown at every Completed or Cancelled ending, and the unreadable tab only at those same endings. So S-004 uses the new hook 'hide' mode: it collapses LargestFilesTab and calls the window's EnsureSelectedTabIsVisible. The guard selected UnreadableTab and kept the tabs visible. UnreadableList is in view with ≥1 full row; LargestFilesList reads inView=false, fullRows=0. Passed.

S-005: a Could not read ending for a missing root of about 1,400 characters, at the floor. No tab is visible and stripRows=0. The texts take the whole panel (378 px, a 575 px extent, scrolling, inView=true); the pre-SL-065 build laid this out at 575 px in a 378 px slot with inView=false. A short missing root at default size shows the panel exactly as tall as its texts. Passed.

S-006: a 140-character root, completed, at 560x644 with the status line shown. The texts scroll inside the 76 px cap (extent well over 116 px). The tabs keep 164 px, over the 154 minimum. The list is in view with ≥1 full row, and CheckFit reports 0 px left over. B-008 (a stopped long-path scan at the floor) also passes with the new checks.

S-007: 12,345 denied folders (one icacls wildcard call each way) at MinWidth 560. The header reads 'Unreadable folders (12,345)' and stripRows=1, both with Largest files selected and with the unreadable tab selected. The caption proves the count reached the window. Passed.

S-008: B-007's tree has 100 largest-file rows. At 560x644 and maximized (1936x1048 laid out, state=Maximized), Cancelled and Completed endings: LargestFilesList.actualHeight ≤ OutcomeTabs.actualHeight, and 2 to 22 of 100 rows built. In S-007, the 12,345-row UnreadableList is 136 px inside 164 px of tabs, with 5 full rows. Passed.

S-008 maximized: on a Cancelled ending the tabs grow from 187 px at the floor to 491 px, and full rows go from 1 to 21. CheckFit shows 0 px between the tabs and the panel's foot. The same holds with the unreadable tab selected, and on a Completed ending, where the outcome row stays at its 292 px minimum. Passed.

S-009: the first scan has 2 unreadable folders and the tab is never selected, so the list is never laid out. FSA_HOOK_READABLE removes one, then the second scan refills both lists while they are detached. Selecting the tab after the ending shows header '(1)' and exactly 1 full row (not the stale 2). Exit 0 shows the report read the detached lists without throwing. S-003 also covers LargestFilesList being refilled while detached and then shown. Passed.

deviations: 'Keep ONE trigger keyed to OutcomeTabs.Visibility' is implemented as one condition with four setters: row 0 height, row 1 height, the texts' MaxHeight, and OutcomePanel.VerticalAlignment. A WPF Style trigger cannot set properties on other elements. The alignment setter is new: a top-aligned panel sizes itself to the selected section's content, so OutcomeTabs' height would change with the selected tab (breaking C-003's 'identical in both states') and leave a band under the panel (C-010). I reasoned this out; no top-aligned variant was built or measured. Every setter depends only on tab visibility, never on section count or on which tab is selected.

OutcomeTabs.MinHeight is 154, not 'one strip + the largest-files list's minimum' (22+56=78). The caption and column headings now live inside the tab, so the section's minimum is strip 22 + tab border/padding 6 + a 3-line caption, the headings and one 56 px row (126). 78 would leave no row for the list.

The texts' cap is 76 px (a title line plus three detail lines: the whole text of a finished folder scan, measured at 75.16). The design's 'what its trigger gives it today' has no single value (the old row was 100* with MaxHeight = natural height, giving 22 to 95 px). 76 gives 10 px headroom at 560x644 with the worst-case 3-line caption; 64 would give 22 px but would cut a partial line off every finished ending.

EnsureSelectedTabIsVisible runs once after each batch of visibility changes (scan start, ShowOutcome, ShowProblem), not after every single change. ShowOutcome makes the unreadable tab visible before ShowLargestFiles, and a mid-batch call would auto-select the unreadable tab, violating 'never selected automatically'. HideSection clears the selection before collapsing a selected tab, so the selection always moves before the collapse.

Report: added a 'header' key (the tab's text) to LargestFilesTab and UnreadableTab, beyond the design's {visible,selected,inView,actualHeight}. It is additive under schema 1 and lets S-007/S-009 prove the 5-digit count and the refreshed count actually reached the header.

Deleted UnreadableList's MaxHeight=200 as well as its MinHeight: inside a tab it must fill the content area. Deleted the 'Largest files, by space on disk' heading as designed; the ranking basis is now the tab header plus the 'On disk' first column. LargestFilesPanel keeps its x:Name (report key, hook watch) and now holds the caption and column headings inside the tab.
The design named the lists ListView; they are ListBoxes in the code, and the rule's pattern covers both.

Hook additions beyond 'repoint expand' were needed to feed designed shapes the app has no other entry to: hide mode (C-005), FSA_HOOK_BACK (C-003), FSA_HOOK_BEFORE/AFTER/READABLE for rescan (C-004, C-011), FSA_HOOK_MAXIMIZE (C-009/C-010).

CheckTabsKeptHeight skips the two runs where the hook shows the reveal status line. The hook adds that line after the tab click, so the window loses about 22 px between the two readings (measured 187.17 → 170.70 = ¾ of 21.96 on a stopped ending). The same comparison runs, and passes, in the matching runs without the status line.
not_built: Design cases C-012 (a third TabItem), C-013 (keyboard switching) and C-014 (125%/150% scaling) are marked material:false in the design and have no fixture; the rule is written in the XAML comment instead.

No test with four headers (Largest files, Largest folders, By extension, Unreadable folders (N)) at 560: only two tabs exist, O-003 settled that they fit, and the slices that add those sections own the fixture. stripRows is asserted with the two real tabs, including the 5-digit count.

No xUnit twin for the new ScrollViewer rule: it sits below '# settled by SL-065' in .taad/fitness.yaml (the engine added it), and by that file's convention settled entries have no ArchitectureRulesTests Fact. rules-parity counts it as settled and reports AGREE.

The plant rows S09/S10 were not measured through eng/rules-harness/harness.py: the harness exits 2 (CANNOT MEASURE) at this HEAD, before any row runs, for an unrelated reason (see follow-ups). They were measured directly with the engine's taad3.fitness.check on scratch copies planted exactly as the harness would plant them: S09 fired at line 107 and S10 at line 110, both at offset 0 as recorded, with no hit on the clean tree.

tests.note: Before any change, with the artifacts/publish exe as found: TIMEOUT, both inside and outside the tool sandbox. That exe was a 359,040-byte framework-dependent apphost; the machine has no .NET 10 runtime, so it sat on the host's missing-runtime window (title 'FsAnalyser.App.exe'). This, not the environment, is why the build check saw every window case time out.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 publish src/FsAnalyser.App/FsAnalyser.App.csproj -c Release -o <temp>, then eng/read-window.ps1 on a one-file folder with that exe
tests.note: The unchanged source published as a 139,892,376-byte single-file bundle; report-mode run EXIT 0 in 1.5 s. Used as the pre-SL-065 baseline, then deleted.
Republished artifacts/publish and rebuilt the hook. Texts 76/96.44 px, tabs 164 px (154+10), list 98 px with 1 full row, stripRows 1, 0 px left in the panel.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case S-002 (then S-003, S-004, S-005, S-006, S-009, one at a time)

tests.note: 19 s. 'Unreadable folders (12,345)', stripRows 1 in both selections, 12,345-row list bounded at 136 px.
30 s. Maximized 1936x1048: Cancelled tabs go from 187 to 491 px, full rows from 1 to 21, no band left.

Every case passed (C-001..C-014, O-016, L-001..L-003, B-001..B-006, V-001, P-001, T-001..T-006, K-001..K-003, R-001, S-001..S-009) except B-007 and B-008. Each failed one check, CheckTabsKeptHeight, and only in the run that shows the reveal status line (187.17 vs 170.70 px, the line arriving after the click). The test was fixed as recorded in deviations. N-001..N-004 were NOT RUN: opt-in network cases.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case B-007 ; then -Case B-008
tests.note: After the fix: B-007 in 48 s, B-008 in 30 s. The height is kept across the click in every run without the status line (164.84, 349.17, 164.00, 187.17 px); the status runs print why they are not compared.
H-001 and H-002 pass; they load WindowCases.ps1's helpers by name.

Exit 2, CANNOT MEASURE, before any row ran: 'the clean baseline is not clean... fitness rules that did not run: [the provider does not use the code it checks]'. That is a must_not_import rule on tests/CfProvider, which the engine reports as UNRAN when the scratch copy has no code graph. It is untouched by this slice. The kept scratch was deleted afterwards.

tests.command: taad3.fitness.check on scratch copies of .taad/fitness.yaml + MainWindow.xaml (clean, and planted with S09+S10 as harness.py inserts them)
tests.note: Clean: no hit from the new rule and no other rule hit. Planted: hits at line 107 (S09, span 107-109) and 110 (S10, span 110-113), offset 0 in both, matching lines.fitness=0. This shows the (?s) pattern matches across line breaks in the engine.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 build FsAnalyser.slnx -c Release

tests.note: AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 47 settled entries.

Real input through the shipped exe: EXIT 0 in 6 s; Completed, 77,523 files, 3 unreadable folders. Header 'Unreadable folders (3)' beside Largest files (selected), stripRows 1. Texts 75.16 px shown whole under the 76 cap; LargestFilesList 4 full rows; tree 14 full rows; UnreadableList off screen.
Same real input at 560x644 with the unreadable tab clicked: tabs 164.84 px before and after, UnreadableList 3 full rows, LargestFilesList inView=false with fullRows 0, tree 3 full rows.

follow_ups: WindowCases.ps1 Update-App republishes only when the exe is older than the newest source. A non-bundle apphost (359 KB, framework-dependent) left in artifacts/publish made every window case time out, and SL-065's build check put that down to 'no interactive window station'. Update-App (and read-window) should refuse an exe that is not the single-file bundle, for example by size or by checking for the bundle marker.

eng/rules-harness/harness.py cannot measure at this HEAD: taad3.fitness reports the must_not_import rule 'the provider does not use the code it checks' as UNRAN when the scratch copy has no code graph, and check_clean refuses. Options: call fitness.check(tree, build=True), or teach check_clean about known-unran import rules. Then run S09/S10 through it.

The person-run network pass (N-001..N-004 plus StalledShareTests, docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md) is stale by its own path rule: MainWindow.xaml(.cs), tests/window/FsaWindowHook/** and WindowCases.ps1 all changed here.

The texts cap is a fixed 76 px at every size. A whole-drive ending (volume line wrapping, then elapsed; about 107 px) or one with notes scrolls even when maximized. If the person dislikes that, the rejected taste alternative was a proportional texts row.

Still open for the person (design-slice): should two sections ever be visible at once (a splitter, or a second tab host)? That would change the 'one section = one TabItem' contract before the largest-folders and by-extension slices.

Validate's own obligations O-001 (unselected section adds nothing and reads inView=false) and O-002 (strip stays one row) now have runnable evidence in S-002/B-007 (OutcomeTabs height kept across the click, lists' inView flipped) and S-007 (stripRows=1 with 'Unreadable folders (12,345)').
The largest-folders and by-extension slices should add a four-header stripRows check at MinWidth 560 with the real headers, and their own report keys per the contract in the XAML comment.
